items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: Lieutenant Lion said, this is my band... we started playing, working with the band... Luther, the, the, the officer was paying, money for us to play

ctx.x: Yeah. on his hands, came on with the band, was a good position. And William Foster, you know, all the people, you know. And William Foster said, Bob, you called me Bob, he said, he said, let's come and get the band with us, with the lines. And they brought all them boys, put them on nice, put them shoes, rustling shoes, tanned shoes, they brought them heavy shoes, with them nails on. William said, I can help you. And he said, yeah, Bob. And so they talked to Lieutenant Lyons, I said, Lord have mercy that morning.…

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: Lieutenant Lyons said, well, I think the best, we got to put this fella back in the big band and let Jim play by himself, you understand, in the small band. Yeah, in the small band.

ctx.x: I took a chance, man, walk up there.

Lieutenant, Fire Lieutenant, they named Lieutenant Lyons, too. I said, all right, Robson, you want to play trombone? I said, yes, sir. I said, all right. I said, well, give me a brand new chord on trombone. So I just took it and put it together, you know. But I could pull it up, understand? Well, every day, so after, they had a fella who was working with the band, but it was three or four weeks, and he couldn't even pull his horn up.
